title: Barmbrack Pear Pudding with Whiskey
tagline: Irish tea loaf, soaked in custard, with pears and chestnuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter both sides of each bread slice, using all the butter. Cut the slices in half. Grease nothing else: the butter does the job.
Peel, core and slice the pears into thin wedges. Roughly break up the chestnuts. Layer the bread, pears and chestnuts in a 1.5-litre ovenproof dish, finishing with bread.
Warm the milk and cream in a pan until steaming, not boiling. Whisk the eggs with 60g sugar, the whiskey and mixed spice. Slowly whisk in the hot milk.
Pour the custard over the bread and press down gently. Leave for 15 minutes so the loaf drinks it up. Sprinkle over the remaining 20g sugar.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until the top is crisp and the middle just set with a slight wobble. Rest for 10 minutes before serving warm.
image_prompt: A deep white ceramic baking dish of golden bread pudding, crisp caramelised sugar top with dark fruit-studded bread corners, soft pear slices and chestnut pieces peeking through, a spoonful lifted out to show creamy set custard, a little steam rising, on a rustic wooden table.
alt_text: A baking dish of golden bread pudding with a crisp sugary top, pear slices and chestnuts showing, and a spoonful lifted out.
caption_hook:
Irish barmbrack makes a very good bread and butter pudding. Add pears, chestnuts and a splash of whiskey and it gets dangerous.
Would you pour extra custard on top, or is that greedy?
